Daily Digest · Computer Science

AI Agents Master Real-World Tasks with Video Feedback

Today's papers reveal a turning point: autonomous agents are moving beyond benchmarks to tackle genuine engineering challenges—from robot co-design with physical testing to production-scale recommendation systems. The common thread is closed-loop learning: agents that see real outcomes, adapt models from video and measurement data, and iteratively improve. This shift from simulation to grounded, multimodal feedback represents a fundamental change in how we'll build autonomous systems.

⚡ Highlighted Findings 4 selected · AI-curated
Robotics
Robots Learn Real Design via Physical Testing Loop

RoboBuilder deploys AI coding agents to co-design robot hardware and software, with every simulation-passing design actually built and tested on a physical course. Unlike pure simulation, the system learns from real-world video feedback and measurement data to close the sim-to-real gap.

Of 15 initial designs passing simulation, zero crossed the real course without agent learning from actual runs.
Nehme, Nam, Govind Srinivasan, Ahmed 2611.23855 PDF
Machine Learning
LLM Agents Autonomously Improve Production ML Systems

MLE Agents automate the full ML engineering loop—hypothesis formation, code implementation, training, and evaluation—on industry-scale recommendation systems rather than toy benchmarks. This human-in-the-loop approach demonstrates that autonomous agents can handle the complexity of real production workflows.

LLM agents successfully navigate production-scale recommendation pipelines autonomously.
Li, Liang, Raj 2611.23910 PDF
Computer Vision
Multimodal Models Learn 3D Camera-Object Relations at Scale

Ultimate3D generates synthetic 3D instruction datasets to teach MLLMs precise camera-object geometry—a critical weakness in current vision models. By rendering photorealistic images with exact camera parameters and diffusion-based augmentation, the framework creates large-scale training data preserving geometric accuracy.

Synthetic 3D pipeline enables MLLMs to accurately capture camera viewpoint, orientation, and shot composition.
He, Song, Xu, Tezcan, Zeng 2611.24795 PDF
AI Safety
Purple-Teaming Hardens LLM Agents Against Prompt Injection

PIPETTE uses reinforcement learning to systematically generate indirect prompt injection attacks, then uses these discoveries for adversarial training—a collaborative offensive-defensive framework. This scales red-teaming to uncover vulnerabilities before deployment as agents interact with untrusted external data.

Automated RL-based attack generation discovers previously unknown prompt injection vulnerabilities at scale.
He, Wang, Zhang, Asokan 2611.24362 PDF

Featured Researcher
GN
Ghadi Nehme
AI Research Engineer · MIT

Nehme's research bridges the sim-to-real gap through interactive learning and physical validation. RoboBuilder represents a paradigm shift: rather than hoping simulation transfers to reality, agents learn from actual hardware feedback to close the gap iteratively. This work directly addresses one of robotics' hardest problems and demonstrates how modern AI can tackle genuine engineering challenges.
